lesson.title: Learn: period, or comma + and / but

items.title: A comma alone is not enough
lines: Two full sentences need a period.
chips: ✅ It was raining hard. There was a strong wind.
❌ It was raining hard, there was a strong wind.
✅ It was raining hard; there was a strong wind.

items.text: Which is correct?
options: Thunder clouds rolled by, flashes of lightning lit the sky.
Thunder clouds rolled by. Flashes of lightning lit the sky.
items.why: Two sentences → period, not just a comma.

items.title: Or: comma + and / but
lines: The comma goes BEFORE and / but.
chips: It was raining hard, and there was a strong wind.
It was late, but he didn't care.

items.text: Which is correct?
options: I refused Alicia's help, she became very angry.
I refused Alicia's help, and she became very angry.

items.title: Informal choices
lines: You may start a sentence with And / But. Very short? The comma can go.
chips: It was raining hard. And there was a strong wind.
It was late. But he didn't care.
It was raining hard and there was a strong wind.

lines: Two complete sentences: use a period (or a semicolon). Never only a comma.
Or join them: sentence + , and / , but + sentence.

examples.text: It was raining hard. There was a strong wind.
It was raining hard, and there was a strong wind.
It was late, but he didn't care.

levels.title: Both… and, either… or
levels.full: Paired Conjunctions: Both … And; Not Only … But Also; Either … Or; Neither … Nor

items.title: Four pairs
lines: They add emphasis.
chips: both … and … (A + B)
not only … but also … (A + B, surprise!)
either … or … (A or B)
neither … nor … (not A, not B)

items.title: Which verb?
lines: both … and → plural. The others → look at the closer subject.
chips: Both my mother and my sister are here.

lines: The same form after each half.

talk.title: Looking for a room
talk.task: Write a short post: you are looking for a room, a pet, or a car. Claude checks it.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English writing partner. Ask me to write a short social-media post (4-6 clear sentences) about something I am looking for: a room to rent, a used car, a pet, a study partner. I should use parallel structure (neat, clean, and quiet), a paired conjunction (both ... and / either ... or), and correct punctuation between sentences. Then check: same form in each list, commas for three items, a period (not only a comma) between two complete sentences, and subject-verb agreement with paired conjunctions.
